description:
The image displays a false-colour infrared satellite map of a mountainous European landscape, consistent with regions like the Alps or Pyrenees. Dense vegetation, such as forests, appears dark red, while sparser vegetation like grasslands shows as lighter red or pink. Exposed rock or bare ground areas are represented by light pink, grey, or white tones.

The map features various land cover classes delineated by dark brown outlines and labelled with four-digit CORINE Land Cover (CLC) codes:
*   `3110`: Broad-leaved forest, visible as extensive dark red areas across the slopes.
*   `3210`: Natural grasslands, appearing as lighter red/pink patches, particularly prominent on mid-slopes.
*   `3310`: Moors and heathland, present in the upper right quadrant.
*   `3400`: Sparsely vegetated areas, including mixed rough grassland, located at mid-to-high elevations.
*   `4100`: Inland wetlands, such as peat bogs, found as a small patch on the right.
*   `4212`: Exposed rock and scree, indicative of high mountain terrain, often mixed with other vegetation.
*   `4220`: Exposed rocks, appearing as lighter, less vegetated areas.
*   `5200`: Alpine and subalpine grasslands, located above the main forest line, in both the upper left and upper right sections.
*   `6100`: Inland waters, likely non-permanent water bodies, visible as a small grey/white patch near the centre-bottom.

A prominent dotted white line traverses the map from the top-middle to the bottom-centre, segmenting the landscape into distinct vegetation zones, consistent with a theoretical tree line. Above this line, alpine grasslands (5200) and exposed rock (4220, 4212) are more prevalent. Below the line, broad-leaved forests (3110) dominate. The spatial pattern illustrates an altitudinal zonation of land cover, transitioning from dense forests at lower elevations to natural grasslands, sparsely vegetated areas, and exposed rocks at higher altitudes.
